tier_reason: The README's Comparisons section compares Snowshoe with OpenSSL 1.0.1e (ecp_nistp256.c). It gives an indirect '~6x faster' estimate built on Kasper's paper, plus the author's own approximate OpenSSL `make tests` timings ('roughly 100 usec' keygen, 4x slower; 'roughly 400 usec' EC-DH, 8x slower). The Snowshoe side has public bench code (tests/ecmul_test.cpp, tests/snowshoe_test.cpp, Makefile clang++ -m64 -O4, median of 10,000 RDTSC runs, CPUs named). The OpenSSL run gives no machine or flags and ships no harness, so this is first-party partial methodology: C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'Kasper demonstrates that the improvements in the paper are roughly 3x faster than normal OpenSSL, pegging Snowshoe roughly 6x faster than OpenSSL 1.0.1e for the same security level' (an indirect estimate). It also says the author's own OpenSSL 1.0.1e `make tests` run (64-bit, ectest.c timing macros enabled) showed 'roughly 100 usec to generate a key (4x slower)' and 'roughly 400 usec for EC-DH (8x slower)'. Both ratios are stated verbatim on the page, not derived. The same page says Crypto++ 5.6.2 and LibTomCrypt 1.17 ECC-256 are 'roughly 20x slower than Snowshoe'.
corrections.hardware: Snowshoe's own RDTSC runs, Turbo Boost off: Core i5-2557M (MacBook Air), Core i5-2500S (iMac) and Core i7 620M (Windows 7 laptop). The page does not say which machine ran OpenSSL 1.0.1e. The i7-2600 and i7-3770 figures on the page are Longa's implementation numbers, not Snowshoe-vs-OpenSSL.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Snowshoe side: Makefile default clang++ -m64 with OPTFLAGS -O4 (make ecmultest / make release); a GCC alternative, -O3 -fomit-frame-pointer -funroll-loops, is commented out. OpenSSL 1.0.1e side: default 64-bit build, flags unstated.
corrections.caveats: The OpenSSL 1.0.1e baseline (2013) is over a decade old. The '6x' figure is an indirect estimate that chains Kasper's paper (about 3x over stock OpenSSL on Core 2) with the author's projected Snowshoe cycle counts. The 4x/8x figures come from the author's own rough OpenSSL run ('roughly' 100/400 usec) on an unstated machine, with no harness in the repo. On the same page some competing 128-bit curve implementations beat Snowshoe on some operations: Longa ecmul_gen/ecmul/ecsimul_gen, Kummer ecmul 72kcy, kumfp127g ecmul and Hamburg ecmul_gen per the page's labels. The BSD-3-Clause LICENSE was added only in 2018 (PR #3). Custom non-standard curve.

notes: Real entry, accurate apart from a mislabel: the 4x/8x ratios were marked '(derived from page data)' but the README states them outright. The hardware field wrongly mixed in Longa's CPUs. Metadata checked: BSD-3-Clause, not archived, not a fork, 64 stars, last commit 2018-02-03, so abandoned is correct.
